items.followUp: What is the main difference between the nutrition of fungi and plants?

rubric.why: Identifies a plant-like feature that led some biologists to place fungi in Plantae.
rubric.description: Fungi have cell walls and are non-motile.
rubric.how: Award for identifying either plant-like feature.

rubric.why: Identifies why other biologists disagreed with placing fungi in Plantae.
rubric.description: Fungi lack chlorophyll and are heterotrophic, unlike plants that make food by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for stating both that fungi lack chlorophyll and that they are heterotrophic.

modelAnswer: Some biologists placed fungi in kingdom Plantae because they have cell walls and are non-motile.
Other biologists disagreed because fungi lack chlorophyll and are heterotrophic; they cannot make their own food by photosynthesis.

items.followUp: How does changing light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: States the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentration when it is a limiting factor.
rubric.description: As carbon dioxide concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided carbon dioxide is limiting.
rubric.how: Award for linking an increase in carbon dioxide concentration with an increase in photosynthesis rate.

rubric.why: Explains why the rate does not keep increasing indefinitely as carbon dioxide concentration rises.
rubric.description: The rate eventually reaches a maximum and levels off because another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the rate plateaus and identifying another limiting factor.

modelAnswer: As carbon dioxide concentration increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided carbon dioxide is a limiting factor.
At a certain concentration, the rate reaches a maximum and levels off because another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a cofactor and an enzyme activator?

rubric.why: Defines cofactors by their non-protein nature and their role in enzyme function.
rubric.description: Cofactors are non protein components required for the activity of some enzymes.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a cofactor as a non protein component needed for enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Distinguishes coenzymes as the organic type of cofactor.
rubric.description: Coenzymes are organic cofactors that assist enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award for identifying coenzymes as organic cofactors.

modelAnswer: Cofactors are non protein components required for the activity of some enzymes; they may be inorganic ions or organic molecules.
Coenzymes are organic cofactors that assist enzyme activity.
